question: A designer asks Claude to create a company logo as a scalable vector graphic that they can drop directly into their design tool. Which output approach is appropriate?
options: A) An inline text description of the logo's appearance, since design tools can convert plain descriptions into vector paths automatically
B) An artifact containing the SVG markup, since SVG images are a supported artifact content type meant for standalone, reusable visual assets
C) A strict tool call to a design_logo tool, since strict tool use is required whenever an image-like asset needs to be generated
D) A structured JSON response describing the logo's colors and shapes, since JSON outputs are the recommended format for any visual design asset
correct_answers: B) An artifact containing the SVG markup, since SVG images are a supported artifact content type meant for standalone, reusable visual assets
explanations: Incorrect. Design tools do not automatically convert prose descriptions into vector paths, so plain text would not give the designer a usable asset.
Correct. SVG images are explicitly a supported artifact type, and a logo the designer will reuse in another tool is exactly the standalone-asset case artifacts handle.
Incorrect. Strict tool use validates parameters passed to a defined tool; it is not a mechanism for generating or delivering image assets.
Incorrect. JSON outputs are meant for structured data fields, not for producing renderable vector graphics that a design tool can import directly.
